'''Usunono Shrine''' (宇須乃野神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=branch shrine}} of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine) within the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} complex. It holds the 14th position among the 16 branch shrines of the Outer Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929), pp. 11–13.</ref>

This article also covers the {{ill|Agata Shrine|ja|県神社|lt=Agata Shrine|lt_ja=縣神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agata Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 縣神社}}, a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|ja|末社|lt=Massha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/minor shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}} of the Outer Shrine, which is co-located with Usunono Shrine.<ref>[[Sengukan Museum]] "[http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area06.php Commemorating the Shikinen Sengu | 125 Shrines Part 5]" (accessed October 10, 2013).</ref><ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929), p. 14.</ref><ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008), p. 52.</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013), p. 64.</ref>

Both shrines are deeply connected to Usuno (宇須乃野), one of the wilderness areas that make up the Yamadahara region.<ref name="ic" />

== Overview ==

{{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}{{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise}} Misano Town, Takabuku (Misanocho Takabuku), Minamiyoseko 2653<ref name="sk0">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): page 370</ref>. Located almost in the center of Misano Town, Takabuku, within a residential area<ref name="ic"/>. Heading from the east exit of {{ill|Miyamachi Station|en|Miyamachi Station|qid=Q1710076|lt=Miyamachi Station}} on the {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line}}, two groves appear toward the settlement of Takabuku; the left is Takabuku Taisha, and the right is Usunono Shrine and Agata Shrine<ref name="ic"/>.

The large {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=Camphor tree}} covering the precincts symbolizes Usunono Shrine and is said to be about 1,000 years old<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>.

The {{ill|Shinto architecture|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shaden (Shrine building)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}} is built in {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style with wooden shingles, surrounded by a {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki}}<ref name="sk0"/>. It features a {{ill|Torii|ja|神明鳥居|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei Torii|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鳥居|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q234731}}<ref name="sk0"/>. There is no {{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Offertory box|qid=Q135491444}}. The precinct area is 1,101 m²<ref name="sk0"/>.

== Usunono Shrine ==

The name "Usunono" refers to the wilderness area around the shrine<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>.

The {{ill|Kami|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami|qq=}} is Usunome-no-Mikoto (宇須乃女命)<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. A deity of {{ill|Bumper crop|en|Bumper crop|qid=Q4997332|lt=Bountiful harvest}}<ref name="ic"/>. According to 'Jinmyo Hisyo,' identified as "Gokokureijin," while 'Ise Watarai-gun Takabuku Village Takabuku Shrine Record' refers to "Goshinrei Niza {{ill|Ukanomitama|ja|宇賀能美多麻神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and Uganome-no-Kami," and 'Jinmyocho Saiko' mentions "also known as {{ill|Kaya-no-hime|ja|草野姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kayano-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カヤノヒメ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8191878}}"<ref name="sk0"/>.

== Agata Shrine ==

Agata Shrine is the 2nd-Ranked {{ill|Setsumatsusha|ja|末社|lt=Massha|2=ja|3=摂末社|4=zh|5=攝末社|6=es|7=Setsumatsusha|8=fr|9=Setsumatsusha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsu-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 摂末社}} of the outer shrine, following {{ill|Igari Shrine|ja|伊我理神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Igari Shrine|qq=}}<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pages 14-15</ref>.

The enshrined deity is Agata-no-Kami (縣神)<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. The guardian deity of Takabuku's Agata area<ref name="ic"/>.

== History ==

Founded before the compilation of the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} (927), according to the definition of Ise Grand Shrine's branch shrines<ref name="ic2">Ise Culture Publishing (2008): page 22</ref>. The name "Usunono Shrine" appears in the same text<ref name="sk0"/>. Also listed as "Takakawara Shrine" in the 'Toyuke Miya Ritual Book'<ref name="sk0"/>, indicating existence before 804 (Enryaku 23)<ref name="ic2"/>. According to 'Ise Watarai-gun Takabuku Village Takabuku Shrine Record,' the shrine was rebuilt multiple times, using Takabuku Taisha as a reference point<ref name="sk0"/>.

Worship declined, and the shrine site became unknown during the early modern period, but it was revived at its current location in 1663 (Kanbun 3)<ref name="sk0"/>. The shrine was rebuilt in March 1911 (Meiji 44)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): page 12</ref>, renovated again in October 1958 (Showa 33), and extensively restored on November 12, 1982 (Showa 57)<ref name="sk0"/>.

== Rituals ==

{{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} (February 20), {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}} (June 20, December 20), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}} (October 20), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} (November 26) are conducted in the precincts by priests, assistants, and attendants. {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}} (January 1), {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}} (January 3), National Foundation Day Festival (February 11), {{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-hi Kinen-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}} (May 14, August 14), and {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}} (December 23) are held remotely<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): page 371</ref>.

== Access ==

When visiting the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine from Miyamachi Station or Yamada Kamiguchi Station, many people start with Usunono Shrine<ref name="gk"/>.

; Public Transportation
* Kintetsu Yamada Line, Miyamachi Station: approx. 15-minute walk<ref name="sk0"/>.
* JR Sangū Line, Yamada Kamiguchi Station: approx. 21-minute walk (1.7 km).
* {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} Bus "Takabuku Kita" Stop: approx. 5-minute walk<ref name="sk0"/>.

; By Car
* {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway}} Ise Nishi IC: via {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 32|ja|三重県道32号伊勢磯部線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 32 Ise Isobe Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357920}} and {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 60|ja|三重県道60号伊勢松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 60 Ise Matsusaka Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11358021}}, approx. 11 minutes (5.1 km).
